sn48.40:1.1: Here the faculties are correlated with the absorptions. Though some correlations are obscure, this passage highlights the connection between the feelings and the practice of the path. | The title is obscure. The commentary says it refers to the sequence in which the feeling faculties are taught here, which accords with the special teaching, rather than the normal sequence. It is noteworthy, however, that a key term of the Sutta is the verb _uppajjati_, which is presented in each section as present tense, past participle, and future tense.
sn48.40:1.4: They experience pain in the body while meditating.
sn48.40:1.6: Here _nimitta_ clearly means “basis”, as also at eg. [an2.77]().
sn48.40:2.1: The sense of this is unclear. Perhaps as the meditator’s first absorption weakens they become conscious of how close the suffering of the sensory world is, and long for higher states.
sn48.40:3.1: Here the faculty of “pleasure” (_sukha_) seems to be equated with “rapture” (_pīti_), and “happiness” (_somanassa_) with “bliss” (also _sukha_).
